description: BC Crew is building RelayNet: an autonomous, decentralized, zero-infrastructure peer-to-peer mesh communications protocol. Designed for mission-critical exploration, disaster response, and off-grid multi-agent telemetry where cellular, satellite, and internet infrastructure are unavailable.
summary:
RelayNet is an autonomous, decentralized, zero-infrastructure Mobile Ad-Hoc Network (MANET) and tactical navigation system engineered for Martian surface exploration (EVAs/Marswalks). On Mars, astronauts face extreme isolation: there is zero GPS, no cellular towers, and a 4-to-24 minute latency lag to Earth. When moving through rugged terrain like craters or canyon rims, direct line-of-sight to the habitat or rover is severed. 

RelayNet transforms astronaut mobile tablets, rovers, and sensor beacons into self-healing, multi-hop relay nodes using Wi-Fi Direct and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). It integrates: (1) relative Martian surface waypoint and hazard beacon tracking without GPS, (2) sub-100ms Push-to-Talk (PTT) tactical voice streaming designed for pressurized space suit gloves, (3) on-device NLP emergency triage, and (4) store-and-forward mesh routing. RelayNet ensures that no human explorer on Mars is ever out of reach, preserving crew safety and mission success during planetary science operations.
details:
# 1. What does RelayNet do and how does it work?

RelayNet 2.0 is an autonomous, decentralized telecommunications and situational-awareness protocol built for extravehicular surface operations (EVAs) on Mars. Using commercial off-the-shelf mobile hardware, RelayNet leverages high-throughput Wi-Fi Direct alongside ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to create a spontaneous, self-healing Mobile Ad-Hoc Network (MANET).

When astronauts disembark from a Mars Base or Rover to conduct geological science (such as sampling Mount Sharp or Jezero Crater), RelayNet links the spacesuit tablets, rovers, and stationary relay markers into an encrypted mesh. Messages, voice notes, and coordinate telemetry hop dynamically from node to node without requiring internet, cellular towers, or orbiting relay satellites.

# 2. How does it address the "Martian Map" Challenge?

• Zero-GPS Relative Navigation: Earth GPS does not exist on Mars. RelayNet carries localized topographic waypoints, geological points of interest, and shelter coordinates across the ad-hoc mesh. Moving astronaut pairs receive real-time relative distance, direction, and RSSI proximity to adjacent teammates and rovers.

• Hazard & Resource Telemetry: The protocol accommodates telemetry packets (suit oxygen levels, battery status, radiation alerts, and localized dust storm fronts) and dynamically surfaces them to the crew.

• Glove-Friendly Tactical PTT Audio: Pressurized astronaut spacesuit gloves make typing coordinates hazardous and slow. RelayNet features a massive tactile Push-to-Talk (PTT) Walkie-Talkie interface with AMR-NB compression, streaming sub-100ms voice notes between disconnected explorers.

• Store-and-Forward Delay Tolerance: Craters and basalt canyon walls cause radio shadowing. RelayNet incorporates Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) architecture: if line-of-sight is blocked, packets are stored in an offline Room database and automatically forwarded the instant a rover or peer comes within radio range.

# 3. Intended Impact & Safety Benefits

Astronaut safety is NASA's top priority. During a life-threatening crisis (suit decompression, fall, or sudden dust storm), RelayNet's on-device NLP triage engine classifies emergency distress keywords in milliseconds—elevating SOS broadcasts to top priority across all relay nodes without waiting for a 20-minute round-trip authorization from Earth ground control.

# 4. Tools, Languages, Hardware & Architecture

• Languages & Frameworks: Kotlin 1.9, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines & Kotlin Flow, Android Architecture Components (MVVM).

• Radio Protocols: Google Nearby Connections API, Wi-Fi Direct (P2P), Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) peripheral/central scanning.

• Audio Engineering: Android native MediaRecorder & AudioTrack utilizing Adaptive Multi-Rate Narrowband (AMR-NB) at 8 kHz sampling, creating lightweight 2-3 KB voice payloads.

• Security & Cryptography: Localized Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) key agreement coupled with AES-CTR zero-trust symmetric encryption anchored in Android KeyStore.

• Energy Optimization: Pure OLED pitch-black dark interface cutting display battery consumption by over 60%, directly extending operational spacesuit tablet survival.
